title: The 50 richest families in America are betting on this trend
summary: An episode of the My First Million podcast (#828) where hosts Shaan Puri and Sam Parr interview billionaire software entrepreneur Joe Liemandt about the ~$1 billion of his own money he has put into Alpha School, a tech-driven private school model. No transcript was available, so this summary is built from the episode title, description, and timestamped show notes only. The framing is that wealthy American families are betting on a new approach to education; the conversation covers Liemandt's intensity-driven operating philosophy, why he's going public with the project now, and a side discussion on AI's effect on cognition. It's a business/philosophy interview, not a technical walkthrough.

title: A Billionaire investor just told me where he's putting his money right now
summary: This is episode 827 of the My First Million podcast, a ~1h45m conversation in which Shaan Puri interviews billionaire value investor Mohnish Pabrai about the mental models behind his investing. No transcript was available, so this summary is built from the title, description, and timestamped show notes only. The discussion covers Pabrai's core principles — introducing randomness, copying winning ideas, going an inch wide and a mile deep, avoiding Excel, waiting for 'fat pitches' — plus his 2026 stock picks, lessons from paying $650,000 to lunch with Warren Buffett, and the cautionary tale of investor Rick Guerin. The takeaway is a set of repeatable mental models for concentrated, patient value investing rather than any software or technical demonstration.

Effort
summary:
RT by @bcherny: Also out today: You can now directly configure the effort level and adaptive thinking in Code (/effort) and Cowork!

Effort allows you to tune Claude's intelligence vs token spend, trading off capability for faster speed and lower costs.

Opus 4.8 respects effort levels strictly, especially at the low end. At low and medium, the model scopes its work to what was asked rather than going above and beyond. This is a good option to control spend and cost, but for more complex work we do recommend High and above - your outputs will probably be better.
